headline: CUT the '2 million visitors (2018)' figure from every description variant: it is in none of the cached sources (Wikipedia has no visitor figure now; Wikivoyage has none either; VisitNSW none). Unsupported.
FIX patrols: VisitNSW (2026) says Main, Clarkes and Wategos are patrolled year-round; Wikivoyage's 'Wategos only at Christmas' is older and contradicted. Do not say Wategos is Christmas-only.
CUT Bluesfest: VisitNSW says Bluesfest and Splendour in the Grass are cancelled or on hiatus. Schoolies stays (WP, WV).
FIX bestTimeBlurb variant 1: 'driest' is wrong for Sep-Nov. Monthly rain (WP): Jul 96, Aug 75, Sep 47, Oct 96, Nov 93 mm. Only September is the driest month.

claims.text: 772 km north of Sydney / 165 km south of Brisbane
claims.source: WP lead (772 km / 165 km). Note Wikivoyage says ~800/175 km; use WP.

claims.text: Cape Byron is the easternmost point of mainland Australia
claims.source: WP, WV, NPWS ('most easterly point of the Australian mainland').

claims.text: 3.7 km Cape Byron walk
claims.source: NPWS Walgun page '3.7km loop', Grade 3, 'a good two hours'; VisitNSW 3.7-kilometre; WV 3.7 km loop.

claims.text: Population 6,330 (2021)
claims.source: WP infobox and lead, 2021 census.

claims.text: around 2 million visitors a year (2018 figure)
claims.source: Not found in WP, WV or VisitNSW as cached. Remove the sentence/clause.
claims.fix: Delete 'around 2 million of them a year (2018 figure)' / 'draws around 2 million visitors a year (2018 figure)' / 'Around 2 million people visit each year (2018 figure).'

claims.text: Cavvanbah, 'meeting place'; Bundjalung Country; Cook named the cape 1770
claims.source: WP history section.

claims.text: Julian Rocks about 2.5 km offshore, temperate and tropical waters merge, marine park dive site
claims.source: WP ('Julian Rocks, 2.5 kilometres from the town and part of the Cape Byron Marine Park'; 'Temperate and tropical waters merge here'); VisitNSW 2.5 km.

claims.text: wellness and alternative scene; surf, diving, whale watching, laid-back lifestyle
claims.source: WV intro; VisitNSW wellness section.

claims.text: Hinterland: Crystal Castle, Bangalow, Mullumbimby
claims.source: VisitNSW names Crystal Castle & Shambhala Gardens; WV and visitbyronbay.com name Bangalow, Mullumbimby, Brunswick Heads.

claims.text: Whale season June-October (tag); peak July-September; best September-October
claims.source: Wild Byron (byronbay.com): 'daily tours between June and October'; VisitNSW: 'peak months are July to September'; WV: 'September and October are the best'. June-October is the defensible tag window; November is unsupported (so bestTimeBlurb v1 'humpbacks still passing' overstates for November).

claims.text: Lighthouse parking $10/hour, max 1 hour per vehicle per day
claims.source: NPWS lighthouse and Walgun pages: '$10 per vehicle per hour ... Maximum 1 hour per vehicle per calendar day, including all NPWS annual passholders'.

claims.text: $5/hour at The Pass
claims.source: NPWS: 'Bawaii rest area, Cosy Corner, and The Pass: $5 per vehicle/motorcycle per hour'.

claims.text: Tip A1 'most people walk up from town along the beach, which takes about 20 minutes'
claims.source: WV: 'about 20 min from the parking at the start of the walk along the beach' (from the car park at the start of the track, not from the town centre).
claims.fix: Parking at the lighthouse is paid and capped at one hour per vehicle per day ($10 an hour, NPWS), so many people park at the start of the track and walk the beach, about 20 minutes to the lighthouse.

claims.text: Tip A2 traffic / Lennox Head exit / airports / 'There is no train'
claims.source: WV: Ewingsdale Road slow, Lennox Head exit at Ross Lane, Ballina/Byron airport ~30 min, Gold Coast ~1 hr: ok. But trains: WP/WV say the Byron line is closed apart from a short solar shuttle; VisitNSW says the North Coast train runs Sydney to Casino with a coach transfer, so 'no train' is misleading.
claims.fix: Replace 'There is no train,' with 'Trains from Sydney stop at Casino, with a coach on to Byron;'

claims.text: Tip A3 'Main Beach is patrolled all summer, but Wategos and other beaches only over the Christmas school holidays'
claims.source: WV (older): Main all summer, others at Christmas. VisitNSW (current): 'Main, Clarkes and Wategos beaches are patrolled year-round'. Conflict; VisitNSW is newer. Winter max 19.4 C (WP) is ok.
claims.fix: VisitNSW lists Main, Clarkes and Wategos as patrolled year-round, so swim between the flags at one of those; winter days reach only about 19 C.

claims.text: Tip B1 Schoolies late Nov to early Dec
claims.source: WV 'Schoolies. In late November/early December ... may be a time to avoid'; WP agrees.

claims.text: Tip B1 'Easter brings the Bluesfest crowds'
claims.source: VisitNSW: 'Splendour in the Grass and Bluesfest have been cancelled or are on hiatus'. WP/WV Bluesfest-at-Easter is stale.
claims.fix: Late November to early December is Schoolies week, which Wikivoyage suggests may be a time to avoid.

claims.text: Tip B2 'Wategos is patrolled only over the Christmas school holidays'
claims.source: Contradicted by VisitNSW (patrolled year-round).
claims.fix: Cut tip B2 or use the A3 fix above.

claims.text: Tip B3 lighthouse carpark limited at weekends, per-hour charge with 1-hour daily max, park can close for weather or fire
claims.source: NPWS Walgun page ('busy place on the weekend, so parking might be limited'); NPWS lighthouse page (open all hours, may close for poor weather or fire danger).

claims.text: bestTimeBlurb v1 '{months} is the driest and mildest stretch, with humpbacks still passing the cape'
claims.source: WP rainfall: Sep 47, Oct 96, Nov 93 mm vs Aug 75, Jul 96, May 99. Only September is driest; Oct and Nov are no drier than July or May. Whales: June-Oct (operator), November unsupported.
claims.fix: Prefer variant 2 ('September is the driest month (47 mm), whale watching is at its best in September and October...') which is supported. If v1 is used: '{months} avoids the summer heat and school-holiday traffic, with September the driest month and humpbacks passing until about October.'

claims.text: bestTimeBlurb v2
claims.source: WP 47 mm September; WV best whale watching Sept-Oct. 'Summer afternoons still weeks away' is loose for November but harmless.

claims.text: bestTimeBlurb v3 summer highs near 27 C, heavier rain
claims.source: WP: Dec-Feb mean max 26.7-28.0 C, Jan/Feb ~165 mm.

claims.text: Taglines 1-3
claims.source: WV, WP, NPWS, VisitNSW.

claims.text: WhyVisit A/B/C reasons and highlights
claims.source: NPWS, WV, VisitNSW (see claims above). B3 humpbacks ok. C3 hinterland ok.

preferred_variants.description: Variant 1 with the visitor clause removed: 'Byron Bay is a beachside town of 6,330 people (2021 census) in the far north-east corner of New South Wales, 772 km north of Sydney and 165 km south of Brisbane. Cape Byron, the headland beside it, is the easternmost point of mainland Australia. People come for the surf beaches, diving at Julian Rocks, whale watching and a wellness and alternative scene. The traditional name for the place is Cavvanbah, "meeting place".'
goodToKnow: Parking at the lighthouse is paid and capped at one hour per vehicle per day ($10 an hour, NPWS), so many people park at the start of the track and walk the beach, about 20 minutes to the lighthouse.

Ewingsdale Road into town is slow in school holidays and summer; Wikivoyage suggests leaving the M1 at the Lennox Head exit (Ross Lane) and coming in from the south. Trains from Sydney stop at Casino, with a coach on to Byron; the nearest airports are Ballina Byron Gateway (about 30 minutes) and Gold Coast (about an hour).
Main, Clarkes and Wategos beaches are patrolled year-round (VisitNSW), so swim between the flags at one of those; winter days reach only about 19 C.
preferred_variants.bestTimeBlurb: Come in {months}: September is the driest month (47 mm), whale watching is at its best in September and October, and summer afternoons are still weeks away.

spots.name: Cape Byron Lighthouse
spots.source: NPWS lighthouse page: lawn 8am-sunset, Maritime Museum in former keeper's office 10am-4pm daily, views, turtle/dolphin/humpback sightings.
spots.ticketUrl: ok: https://www.nationalparks.nsw.gov.au/things-to-do/historic-buildings-places/cape-byron-lighthouse (200, title 'Cape Byron Lighthouse | NSW National Parks')

fields.hours: Lawn 8:00 AM - sunset; museum 10:00 AM - 4:00 PM
fields.note: No cost field correct: the $10/hour charge is parking.

spots.name: Cape Byron Walk
spots.source: NPWS Walgun page: 3.7 km loop, Grade 3, rainforest, clifftops, beaches, lighthouse, whales in season; open all hours but may close for weather or fire.
spots.ticketUrl: ok: https://www.nationalparks.nsw.gov.au/things-to-do/walking-tracks/walgun-cape-byron-walking-track (200, title 'Walgun Cape Byron walking track | NSW National Parks')

fields.free: true is fine when walking in from town; NPWS says park entry fees apply at the lighthouse carpark. Optional hours: 'Open 24 hours; may close for weather or fire danger'.

spots.name: Main Beach
spots.source: VisitNSW: Main Beach patrolled year-round; WV: patrolled all summer. Bio says 'patrolled' only, which holds.

spots.name: Wategos Beach
spots.source: 'Sheltered' is not in sources. WV: north side of the point, cult longboard crowd, common dolphins not uncommon among surfers; VisitNSW: patrolled year-round; Little Wategos is Australia's easternmost beach.
spots.fix_bio: A beach on the north side of Cape Byron with a longboard following, where common dolphins are not uncommon among the surfers.

spots.name: The Pass
spots.source: VisitNSW: The Pass and The Wreck two of Australia's most famous surf breaks, Soul Surf School lessons; WV: Clarkes Beach lies east of Main Beach 'but before the Pass'. So The Pass is at the far (eastern) end of Clarkes, not its 'southern end'; the writer's 'southern end of Clarkes Beach' is unsupported. 'Surfers' lookout' unsupported. NPWS: $5/hour parking.
spots.fix_bio: A long-board surf break at the end of Clarkes Beach, which VisitNSW names among Australia's most famous surf breaks.

spots.name: Julian Rocks
spots.source: WV five minutes by boat, 5-25 m; VisitNSW 2.5 km offshore, tours by Sundive, Wild Byron, Out of the Blue. No ticketUrl is correct (many operators).

spots.name: Crystal Castle and Shambhala Gardens
spots.source: crystalcastle.com.au: 'Open Every Day 10am - 5pm', last entry 4pm, closed Good Friday, Christmas Day and Boxing Day; address 81 Monet Drive, Montecollum.
spots.ticketUrl: ok: https://crystalcastle.com.au/ (200, title 'Crystal Castle Byron Bay | Giant Crystals, Gardens & Attractions')

fields.hours: 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM (last entry 4:00 PM); closed Good Friday, Christmas Day and Boxing Day
fields.cost: Adult price not shown on the cached homepage; keep cost omitted.

spots.name: Brunswick Heads
spots.source: visitbyronbay.com surrounding towns: 'one of the gems of the far north coast of New South Wales', river village on the Brunswick River, ~20 min up the motorway; WV 'nice day trip'.

spots.name: Bangalow
spots.source: 'Well-preserved nineteenth-century main street' is not stated anywhere. WP: 'historic streetscape', town appeared in the 1880s, main street lined with cafes and boutique shops, heritage buildings. WV: 'nice relaxed old-town main street'.
spots.fix_bio: A hinterland village founded in the 1880s, with a historic main street of cafes and boutique shops.

spots.name: Mullumbimby
spots.source: WP: town in Byron Shire at the foot of Mount Chincogan; WV and visitbyronbay.com list it among hinterland towns to visit.

spots.name: Tallow Beach
spots.source: 'Birdwatching and whale watching' IS supported: NPWS Arakwal page, 'Tallow Beach is 3.2km from the heart of Byron Bay and a great place for swimming, birdwatching, whale watching'. 'Long' and 'to Broken Head' supported (visitbyronbay beaches: stretches south all the way to Broken Head; WV 'very long'). 'South-facing' is unsupported: WV says it is on the south side of the Byron headland.
spots.fix_bio: A long beach running south from Cape Byron towards Broken Head, reached through Arakwal National Park, for swimming, birdwatching and whale watching.

spots.name: Arakwal National Park
spots.source: NPWS Arakwal page: co-managed by NPWS and the Bundjalung of Byron Bay (Arakwal) people, 3 km of beach, always open but may close for storm or fire. 'Bush trail' not verified; safer wording below.
spots.ticketUrl: ok: https://www.nationalparks.nsw.gov.au/visit-a-park/parks/arakwal-national-park (200, title 'Arakwal National Park | NSW National Parks')
spots.fix_bio: A small national park behind Tallow Beach, jointly managed by the Bundjalung of Byron Bay (Arakwal) people and NPWS, with 3 km of beach backed by dunes and coastal heath.

fields.hours: Always open; may close for storm or fire danger

spots.name: Broken Head Nature Reserve
spots.source: NPWS Broken Head page: rainforest walk to Three Sisters lookout, beaches, whale watching; visitbyronbay beaches names Kings Beach; always open but may close for weather or fire; entry $4 per vehicle per hour.
spots.ticketUrl: ok: https://www.nationalparks.nsw.gov.au/visit-a-park/parks/broken-head-nature-reserve (200, title 'Broken Head Nature Reserve | NSW National Parks')

fields.hours: Always open; may close for poor weather or fire danger (replaces 'Open daily; check current alerts')
fields.cost: Only a $4/vehicle/hour parking-style park entry fee (NPWS); optional, omit as with Cape Byron.

spots.name: Belongil Beach
spots.source: visitbyronbay.com beaches: dogs allowed (as signposted), stretches towards Brunswick Heads, 'area north of Belongil Creek is clothes optional'; WV lists it.

spots.name: The Farm
spots.source: No accepted photo; not mentioned in any text. Not checked further.
